title: Electromagnetic Induction
seo_title: Secondary 4 Physics: Electromagnetic Induction Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Deduce from experiments that a changing magnetic field can induce an e.m.f. in a circuit; state the factors affecting the magnitude of the induced e.m.f. (Faraday's law) and that its direction opposes the change producing it (Lenz's law); describe a simple a.c. generator with slip rings and sketch its output; describe the structure and principle of a transformer and recall and apply Vs/Vp = Ns/Np and VpIp = VsIs for an ideal transformer; explain the use of high voltage for the transmission of electrical energy (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Physics worksheets on electromagnetic induction: Faraday's and Lenz's laws, the a.c. generator, transformers and high-voltage transmission. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A changing magnetic field induces an e.m.f.
key_sub: Transformer: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np; ideal: VpIp = VsIs.
body_html:
How to think about it

A changing magnetic field induces an e.m.f. in a conductor.

  • Larger e.m.f.: faster movement, stronger magnet, more turns (Faraday's law). The induced current opposes the change (Lenz's law).
  • An a.c. generator uses slip rings; turning faster gives a larger peak e.m.f. and a higher frequency.
  • Transformers need a.c.: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np, and for an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs.
  • Transmitting at high voltage means a small current, so less power (I²R) is lost in the cables.
Example

Np = 500, Ns = 25, Vp = 240 V. Vs?

Vs = 240 × 25 ÷ 500

Answer: 12 V

Example

Ideal: 240 V, 0.5 A in; 12 V out. Is?

240 × 0.5 = 12 × Is

Answer: 10 A

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a stationary magnet in a coil induces a current.
  • Thinking a transformer works with d.c.
  • Saying a step-up transformer increases the power. It increases the voltage and decreases the current.
  • Mixing up slip rings (generator, a.c.) and the split-ring commutator (d.c. motor).

faq.q: What affects the size of an induced e.m.f.?
faq.a: How fast the magnetic field changes: the speed of movement, the strength of the magnet and the number of turns on the coil.
An alternating current in the primary coil makes a changing magnetic field in the soft iron core, which induces an alternating e.m.f. in the secondary coil.

faq.q: Why is high voltage used for transmission?
faq.a: The same power at a higher voltage needs a smaller current, and the power lost in the cables (I²R) falls with the square of the current.

items.q: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary coil and 2000 turns on the secondary coil. The primary voltage is 240 V. What is the secondary voltage?
items.e: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np, so Vs = 240 × 2000 ÷ 100 = 4800 V (a step-up transformer).

items.q: A transformer has 500 turns on the primary coil and 10 000 turns on the secondary coil. The primary voltage is 230 V. What is the secondary voltage?

items.q: A transformer changes 12 V to 60 V. The secondary coil has 1000 turns. How many turns are on the primary coil?
